analysis: Both supplied units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines ~425 and ~618), documentation-only with no executable code, no mode changes, and no rename metadata. They describe security-relevant behavior changes made elsewhere in the PR: App Attest dead-key rotation (limits of 1 per hour and 4 per 24h per machine, serialized with machine merges, never revoking or denying serving); a 6-hour enrollment backoff after repeated invalidKey failures; hourly APNs code-identity retries; staging the macOS 27 device-attestation chain; and untrusted ready-reply diagnostics (launch_session, boot_time, operation_stalled_seconds) that sit outside the signed transcript. The changelog also states that public model-demand publication is delayed at least one hour with cohorts under 20 requests or 3 accounts suppressed, and that the diagnostics never affect authorization. The changelog states these as intent only and cannot confirm the corresponding source. Relevant threats are T-053, T-054, T-055, T-057, T-058, and TB-002 and TB-011 for the untrusted diagnostics, TB-009 for the APNs/status paths, and A-015, A-016 and A-017 for the assets. The next review pass should check the actual code, which was not supplied here. In particular: (1) key rotation must demand the full attestation, receipt, build-qualification and assertion checks, and must not let an operator bypass credential continuity or revocation by deliberately triggering a dead-key state; (2) the rotation budget must be race-free against machine merges; (3) the diagnostics must stay excluded from the signed transcript, authorization and fencing decisions; (4) the demand-history suppression must avoid small-cohort re-identification; (5) the admin diagnostics endpoint must stay admin-gated. No findings can be raised from the changelog text alone, and the coverage limit is that the source files were not provided.
